_about: External NL->visualisation test set adapted from David Bull's MSc functional-test tasks (Table 5.1). Each task's natural-language wording is fed to the web NL box; the gold records the expected selection, ER pattern and chart(s). Grade the four layers independently (selection / pattern / chart / filter-join-aggregate). Mondial column names verified against mondial_schema_summary_clean.json (2026-08-26).

tasks.nl_input: The current population of countries in Europe
tasks.expected_filter_join_aggregate: filter continent = 'Europe' (needs join country.code -> encompasses.country, encompasses.continent = 'Europe')
tasks.stresses: geographic filter across a many-many relationship (country<->continent)
tasks.notes: population is the single snapshot country.population, NOT the country_population time series. country is geographical+lexical, so choropleth/word cloud are also eligible.

tasks.nl_input: The relationship between GDP and unemployment for all countries
tasks.stresses: is-a / inherited-key subset (economy PK = country, a FK to country); two scalar attributes -> scatter
tasks.notes: economy.country is both the whole PK and a FK, so the entity is an inherited-key basic entity, treated like a basic entity for charting.

tasks.nl_input: The length of the borders for all countries in South America
tasks.expected_filter_join_aggregate: filter both endpoints to South America (join country1/country2 -> encompasses, continent = 'South America')
tasks.stresses: reflexive many-many (country borders country); geographic filter on BOTH endpoints
tasks.notes: length is the scalar edge weight. The continent filter on a reflexive relationship is the hard part.

tasks.nl_input: The top ten Mexican airports by elevation
tasks.expected_filter_join_aggregate: filter country = 'Mexico' (country code MEX); order by elevation desc; limit 10
tasks.stresses: single-column equality filter + ordering + row limit (top-N)
tasks.notes: airport PK is iata_code alone (own key, not inherited) -> basic entity. elevation is the single scalar measure.

tasks.nl_input: The GMT offset of all countries
tasks.expected_filter_join_aggregate: would require chaining joins country -> province -> city -> airport to attribute a GMT offset to a country
tasks.stresses: multi-hop join chain; the measure (gmt_offset) lives on airport, not country
tasks.notes: David's system FAILED this (needs country-province-city-airport chaining). Interesting probe: does the LLM NL parser overreach (wrongly map to a country measure) or degrade gracefully? Either 'no sensible result' or an honest airport-level chart is acceptable; a confidently-wrong country choropleth is a failure.

tasks.nl_input: All country-city pairs where the population of the city has been at least 5,000,000 at some point
tasks.expected_filter_join_aggregate: aggregate MAX(population) per (country, city) over all years, then filter MAX >= 5000000
tasks.expected_pattern: one_many_relationship (country -> city) / weak temporal on city_population
tasks.stresses: temporal aggregate ('at some point' = MAX over years) + threshold filter; relationship spans first-and-last entity in a chain
tasks.notes: David's system FAILED this. Probe whether the aggregate ('at some point') is understood at all. Graceful failure is an acceptable outcome here.

tasks.nl_input: Countries that are in two continents
tasks.expected_filter_join_aggregate: aggregate: keep countries whose COUNT(distinct continent) = 2 (David used custom SQL for this)
tasks.stresses: many-many relationship; HAVING COUNT = 2 aggregate filter
tasks.notes: Even without the COUNT=2 filter, the core many-many -> sankey/chord recommendation should be correct; grade the count filter separately.

tasks.nl_input: The relationship between industry and service GDP in the economies of different countries
tasks.stresses: is-a subset again; two scalar attributes -> scatter
tasks.notes: industry and service are the two scalar percentages on economy.

tasks.nl_input: Display the population of France, Spain, and Italy for the years 1960 to 2015
tasks.expected_filter_join_aggregate: filter country IN (France, Spain, Italy); filter year BETWEEN 1960 AND 2015
tasks.stresses: temporal weak entity (year is an orderable key) -> line; multi-value IN filter + numeric range filter
tasks.notes: country_population is a weak entity (PK country+year). year is continuous/orderable so a line chart is valid; this is the case David uses to demonstrate 'effectiveness' (order-aware).

tasks.nl_input: Display the history of the population level of each country in Oceania
tasks.stresses: temporal weak entity + geographic filter via a many-many relationship
tasks.notes: 'history' + 'each country' -> one temporal line per country. Continent membership is only reachable through encompasses.

tasks.nl_input: Display the elevation of all airports that are at least 2000 in altitude
tasks.stresses: identity/alternative-key handling: airport NAME is not unique, so the key must be iata_code; single numeric filter
tasks.notes: Good test of the identity-role logic: the chart must key by iata_code (unique), not name. Grade whether the label/key role is iata_code.

tasks.nl_input: Display how the population of continents is divided between countries
tasks.expected_filter_join_aggregate: optionally weight country population by encompasses.percentage; group by continent
tasks.stresses: many-many part-of-whole; David notes this flips between one-many and many-many depending on the data subset
tasks.notes: 'divided between' = part-of-whole -> sankey/treemap. percentage is the natural weight. Accept a one-many hierarchy (treemap/circle packing) reading too.

tasks.nl_input: The languages spoken in South American countries, excluding languages spoken by less than 1,000,000 people on the continent
tasks.expected_filter_join_aggregate: filter continent = 'South America' (join country -> encompasses); exclude languages whose total speakers on the continent < 1,000,000 (percentage x country population, summed per language, thresholded)
tasks.stresses: weak entity (spoken: country+language) + geographic filter + a derived cross-table aggregate threshold (David flagged this as needing considerable SQL updates)
tasks.notes: spoken is a weak entity (strong = country, weak key = language name); percentage is the scalar. The speaker-count threshold is a derived aggregate the NL parser is unlikely to compute fully -> grade the aggregate layer separately from the base grouped-bar recommendation.
